routines.title: Neck & Shoulder Reset
routines.subtitle: Ease the tightness screens leave in your neck.
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Move your head slowly for the first minute. Drink some water, and try putting your screen at eye height for the rest of the day.

routines.title: Foot Relief
routines.subtitle: Ease tired arches after a long day standing.
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Do the other foot even if it does not hurt — feet like to match. Drink some water. If your heel is angry in the morning, roll a frozen water bottle under it for five minutes.

routines.title: Hand & Wrist Reset
routines.subtitle: Undo a day of typing and scrolling.
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Shake your hands out and let them rest. If your fingers go numb or tingly while you work, stand up and move every half hour.

routines.title: Scalp & Sleep
routines.subtitle: An Indian head massage you do lying in bed.
needs: A towel over the pillow if you use oil
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: There is nothing to do at the end. Leave your arms where they land, keep your eyes closed, and let sleep come on its own.

routines.title: Face Lymphatic Glow
routines.subtitle: Feather-light strokes for a puffy morning face.
needs: A drop of facial oil optional
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Drink a glass of water and sit tall for a few minutes. Doing this lightly most mornings does far more than doing it hard once.

routines.title: Jaw & TMJ Release
routines.subtitle: Unclench the jaw you grind all night.
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Keep your lips together and your teeth apart for the rest of the day. Soft food tonight if your jaw feels tired, and a warm flannel on the cheek helps.

routines.title: Sinus & Headache Relief
routines.subtitle: Ease a tight head and blocked sinuses.
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Sip some water and let your eyes rest for a minute. A warm, damp cloth over the face feels very good after this.

routines.title: Forearm Rescue
routines.subtitle: Undo the ache of typing, scrolling and clicking.
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Shake your hands out and drink some water. Give your wrists a few minutes away from the keyboard before you start typing again.

routines.title: Lower Back Ball Release
routines.subtitle: A tennis ball, a wall, and an easier back.
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Stand up slowly and walk around for a minute. A little tenderness tomorrow is normal, like after the gym, and a warm shower helps.

routines.title: Glute & Piriformis Ball
routines.subtitle: Sit on a ball and let a tight hip let go.
needs: A mat if you prefer the floor
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Stand and walk for a minute before you sit down again. A day of tenderness is normal; sharp or shooting pain down the leg is not, so see a doctor if that turns up.

routines.title: Calf & Shin Release
routines.subtitle: Loosen tired calves and aching shins.
needs: A rolled towel or foam roller
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Drink some water and walk about for a minute. If one calf stays swollen, hot or sore afterwards, leave it alone and speak to a doctor.

routines.title: Desk Reset
routines.subtitle: Five quiet minutes at your desk, fully clothed.
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Look out of a window for twenty seconds before you go back to the screen. Grab a glass of water while you are up.

routines.title: Back Basics
routines.subtitle: A calm, whole-back massage anyone can give.
needs: A pillow for under their ankles
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Let them lie still for a minute before they get up. Offer water and keep their back warm. Nothing heavy for the next half hour.

routines.title: Neck & Shoulder Reset
routines.subtitle: Release the tension screens put in your shoulders.
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Sit up slowly. Drink some water. Nothing heavy for the next half hour.

routines.title: Scalp & Head Wind-Down
routines.subtitle: An Indian head massage that ends in sleep.
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Let them lie there as long as they like. If you used oil, shampoo it out before adding water. Keep the lights low and the phones away.

routines.title: Upper Back Knot Hunt
routines.subtitle: Find the knots between the shoulder blades and hold them.
needs: A pillow for under their ankles
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: A worked-over knot can ache for a day, a bit like after the gym — that is normal. Water, a warm shower, and no heavy lifting tonight.

routines.title: Lower Back & Hip Relief
routines.subtitle: Start at the hips, because that is usually the cause.
needs: A pillow for under their hips
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Ask them to roll onto their side before sitting up. Water, a slow short walk, and no heavy lifting today. A little tenderness tomorrow is normal.

routines.title: Foot Ritual
routines.subtitle: Warm towels, slow thumbs, both feet, no rushing.
needs: A pillow for under their knees
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Their feet will be slippery — dry them properly before they stand up. Water, warm socks, and stay off hard floors for a while.

routines.title: Hamstring & Calf Recovery
routines.subtitle: Ease heavy, sore legs after a hard session.
needs: A pillow for under the ankles
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Stand up slowly — the legs will feel loose. Drink some water and walk about for a minute. Leave heavy lifting until tomorrow.

routines.title: Full Body Express
routines.subtitle: Head to toe in twenty unhurried minutes.
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Let them lie still for a minute before sitting up. Water, something warm to wear, and a slow start to whatever is next.

routines.title: Office Chair 10-Minute
routines.subtitle: A proper shoulder rub at a desk, fully dressed.
needs: No oil — everyone stays fully dressed
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Roll the shoulders a few times before standing. Drink some water. Try to move about once an hour for the rest of the day.

routines.title: Hand & Wrist, Seated
routines.subtitle: Six gentle minutes for hands that ache.
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Do the second hand even if only one aches — hands like to match. A warm drink afterwards helps stiff joints.

routines.title: Foot Reflexology, Socks Off
routines.subtitle: Ten minutes for feet that have been standing all day.
needs: A firm cushion for your lap
Socks off — everything else stays on
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Get up slowly and put socks back on — feet cool down fast. Drink some water. Do the second foot the same day if you can.

routines.title: Hand Exchange
routines.subtitle: You both give and both receive, at the same time.
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Shake both hands out and have some water. If one of you is much stronger, agree a lighter number before the next round.

steps.title: Roll your shoulders and breathe
steps.body: Sit tall and roll both shoulders slowly backward. Let them drop a little lower with every breath out.
steps.sensationCue: Loose, easy movement. No pinching at the top of the circle.
steps.rhythm: One slow roll every four seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as your shoulders drop
steps.voiceScript: Sit tall with your feet flat on the floor. Roll both shoulders slowly backward, and let them settle a little lower each time you breathe out. There is no rush at all here.
steps.commonMistake: Do not rush the roll. Slow circles loosen more than fast ones.

steps.title: Warm the side of your neck
steps.body: Rest your right palm on the left side of your neck. Stroke slowly down to the shoulder, then swap hands and sides.
steps.sensationCue: Warm and smooth. Nothing sharp or scratchy.
steps.rhythm: One long stroke every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Slow breath in, slower breath out
steps.voiceScript: Rest your right palm flat against the left side of your neck. Stroke slowly down towards the shoulder, lift off, and start again from the top. After about twenty seconds, swap hands and do the other side.
steps.commonMistake: Do not press hard yet. This step only warms the skin and muscle.
steps.caution: Stay on the soft side of the neck. Never press the front of your throat.

steps.title: Squeeze the top of your shoulder
steps.body: Reach across and grip the ridge of muscle on top of the opposite shoulder. Squeeze, lift it slightly, and let go.
steps.sensationCue: A deep, dull ache that softens as you work. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: About one squeeze per second
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you squeeze
steps.voiceScript: Reach your right hand across to your left shoulder and take that ridge of muscle between your thumb and fingers. Squeeze, lift it a little, then let it go, like kneading dough. Give each side about thirty seconds.
steps.commonMistake: Do not pinch with your fingertips. Use the whole flat of your fingers.

steps.title: Hold the tightest spot
steps.body: Feel along the top of your shoulder for the sorest lump. Press straight down and hold still for thirty seconds each side.
steps.sensationCue: A strong ache that fades by about half while you hold.
steps.rhythm: Still — hold, do not rub
steps.breathCue: Breathe out into the pressure
steps.voiceScript: Feel along the top of your shoulder until you find the sorest little lump. Press straight down into it with your fingertips and simply hold, counting thirty slow seconds. Then ease off and do the other side.
steps.commonMistake: Do not rub the spot. Still, steady pressure is what lets it let go.
steps.caution: If the ache turns sharp, burning or shoots down your arm, come off it.

steps.title: Work the base of your skull
steps.body: Curl your fingertips up under the bony ridge at the back of your head. Make small, slow circles either side of the middle.
steps.sensationCue: A melting release that spreads up into your head. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: Three or four circles, then move a thumb-width
steps.breathCue: Let your head get heavy on your fingers
steps.voiceScript: Curl your fingertips up under the bony ridge at the back of your head, where the skull meets the neck. Make small, slow circles, and let the weight of your head rest into your fingers. Work outward towards your ears a thumb-width at a time.
steps.commonMistake: Do not dig with your nails. Use the soft pads of your fingers.
steps.caution: Stay either side of the bony bumps of the spine, never on them.

steps.title: Roll a ball against the wall
steps.body: Stand with a tennis ball between the wall and the muscle beside your spine. Lean in and roll slowly, pausing where it complains.
steps.sensationCue: Firm pressure you control by how much you lean in. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: Pause ten seconds on any sore spot
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you lean in
steps.voiceScript: Stand with your back to a wall and trap a tennis ball between the wall and the muscle beside your spine. Bend your knees to roll slowly up and down, and stop for ten seconds on anything that complains. Swap to the other side halfway through.
steps.commonMistake: Do not roll fast. Slow beats hard every single time.
steps.caution: Keep the ball off your spine. Stay on the muscle either side of it.

steps.title: Lengthen the side of your neck
steps.body: Drop your left ear towards your left shoulder and rest your left hand on your head. Let its weight hold you there twenty seconds, then swap.
steps.sensationCue: A long, comfortable pull down the side. Never a pinch.
steps.rhythm: Hold twenty seconds each side
steps.breathCue: Breathe out and let the shoulder sink
steps.voiceScript: Drop your left ear towards your left shoulder and lay your left hand gently over your head. Use only the weight of the hand, never a pull, and hold for about twenty seconds. Come up slowly, then do the other side.
steps.commonMistake: Do not lift the opposite shoulder. Let it stay down and heavy.
steps.caution: Never force the stretch. Weight of the hand only, and stop if anything tingles.

steps.title: Rake your fingertips down
steps.body: Draw your fingertips slowly from the base of your skull down your neck and out over the shoulder. Get lighter with every pass.
steps.sensationCue: Shivery and calming, like the work is closing.
steps.rhythm: One slow rake every four seconds, hands alternating
steps.breathCue: Long, easy breaths
steps.voiceScript: Draw your fingertips slowly from the base of your skull, down the neck and out across the shoulder. Alternate hands, and make each pass a little lighter than the one before.

steps.title: Rest your hands and finish
steps.body: Rest both palms on the tops of your shoulders. Take three slow breaths, then let your hands slide away.
steps.sensationCue: Warmth and stillness. Shoulders sitting lower than before.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: Three long breaths out
steps.voiceScript: Cross your hands over and rest a palm on each shoulder. Do not move at all. Take three slow breaths, then let your hands slide down into your lap.
steps.commonMistake: Do not jump straight back to your desk. Give it one quiet moment.

steps.title: Warm the whole foot
steps.body: Cross one ankle over the opposite knee. Sandwich the foot between both palms and stroke firmly from toes to ankle, over and over.
steps.sensationCue: Warmth and blood coming back into a cold foot.
steps.rhythm: One long stroke every two seconds
steps.breathCue: Slow breath out with each stroke
steps.voiceScript: Sit down and cross one ankle over the opposite knee. Sandwich your foot between both palms and stroke firmly from the toes up to the ankle, again and again, until the whole foot feels warm.
steps.commonMistake: Do not rush to the sore spot. Warm the whole foot first.

steps.title: Loosen the ankle
steps.body: Hold your heel still with one hand. With the other, circle the foot slowly five times each way.
steps.sensationCue: Easy movement. No clicking, grinding or pinching.
steps.rhythm: One slow circle every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Keep breathing — do not hold it
steps.voiceScript: Hold your heel still in one hand so the ankle cannot cheat. With the other hand, take the front of the foot and circle it slowly, five times one way and five times back.
steps.commonMistake: Do not swing the whole leg. Only the foot should move.

steps.title: Thumb-walk the arch
steps.body: Press your thumb into the heel and walk it forward along the arch in small bites, like a caterpillar. Make three passes.
steps.sensationCue: Tender spots that ease after a few seconds of pressure.
steps.rhythm: About one small bite per second
steps.breathCue: Breathe out on the tender spots
steps.voiceScript: Press your thumb into the middle of the heel, then bend and straighten it to walk forward along the arch in tiny bites, like a caterpillar. Take three slow passes from heel to the ball of the foot, and pause a few seconds anywhere tender.
steps.commonMistake: Do not slide. Press, ease off, move a little — that is the walk.

steps.title: Stretch the sole open
steps.body: Put both thumbs in the centre of the sole. Draw them slowly apart to open the foot outward, then start again lower down.
steps.sensationCue: The sole broadening. A slow, spreading stretch.
steps.rhythm: One slow spread every five seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you spread
steps.voiceScript: Place both thumbs together in the centre of the sole, with your fingers wrapped over the top of the foot. Draw the thumbs slowly apart so the sole opens outward. Move a little further down and do it again.
steps.commonMistake: Do not go fast. This kind of tissue only gives to slow, patient pressure.

steps.title: Work the heel
steps.body: Make firm circles into the fleshy pad of the heel with your knuckles. Keep the circles small and slow.
steps.sensationCue: Deep, dull and satisfying. Never sharp or burning.
steps.rhythm: About one small circle per second
steps.breathCue: Long breath out as you press in
steps.voiceScript: Make a loose fist and press your knuckles into the fleshy pad of the heel. Work in small, firm circles, covering the whole heel. Keep it slow, and let it be a deep, dull feeling rather than a sharp one.
steps.commonMistake: Do not hammer at it. Sink in slowly and let the pressure build.
steps.caution: Ease right off if you feel a sharp, stabbing pain under the heel.

steps.title: Slide between the foot bones
steps.body: Turn to the top of the foot. Slide your thumb along each groove between the long bones, from the toes back towards the ankle.
steps.sensationCue: Narrow lines of tenderness that ease as you pass.
steps.rhythm: One slow slide per groove
steps.breathCue: Keep your breathing steady
steps.voiceScript: Turn your attention to the top of the foot. Find the grooves between the long bones and slide your thumb along each one, from the base of the toes back towards the ankle. Four grooves, one slow pass each.
steps.commonMistake: Do not press on the bones themselves. Stay in the soft grooves.

steps.title: Pull and circle each toe
steps.body: Take each toe in turn. Pull gently for two seconds, then circle it once each way.
steps.sensationCue: A tiny release in each joint. Never a crack or a wrench.
steps.rhythm: About six seconds per toe
steps.breathCue: Easy breaths, no holding
steps.voiceScript: Take hold of your big toe between your thumb and finger. Pull gently for a couple of seconds, then circle it once each way. Work along all five toes, then give the whole foot a little shake.
steps.commonMistake: Do not yank for a click. A gentle, steady pull is enough.

steps.title: Roll it out with a ball
steps.body: Stand and roll a tennis ball under your foot, from heel to toes. Pause ten seconds on any spot that complains.
steps.sensationCue: Firm pressure you control by how much weight you lean in.
steps.rhythm: One slow pass every five seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you lean your weight in
steps.voiceScript: Stand up and put a tennis ball under the arch of your foot. Roll it slowly from heel to toes, and choose your own pressure by how much weight you let down onto it. When something complains, stop and rest on it for ten seconds.
steps.commonMistake: Do not race the ball back and forth. Slow rolling does the work.
steps.caution: Hold a wall or chair for balance. Keep your weight light if the skin is tender.

steps.title: Stretch the calf
steps.body: Put both palms on a wall and step this foot back. Keep the heel down and lean in for thirty seconds.
steps.sensationCue: A long pull through the back of the calf. Never a sharp grab.
steps.rhythm: Hold thirty seconds, then ease out slowly
steps.breathCue: Breathe out and sink into it
steps.voiceScript: Stand facing a wall and press both palms into it. Step the foot you have been working back behind you, keep that heel flat on the floor, and lean your hips towards the wall. Hold for thirty slow seconds, then come out of it gently.
steps.commonMistake: Do not let the back heel lift. That is where the stretch lives.

steps.title: Finish with long strokes
steps.body: Stroke the whole foot from toes to ankle, getting lighter each time. Then swap feet and work the other side the same way.
steps.sensationCue: Light, warm and finished.
steps.rhythm: One feather-light stroke every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Slow, quiet breaths
steps.voiceScript: Sandwich the foot between your palms one last time and stroke from the toes up to the ankle, getting lighter with every pass. Rest it on the floor and notice how different the two feet feel. Then start again on the other side.
steps.commonMistake: Do not skip the second foot. Feet like to match.

steps.title: Warm your hands
steps.body: Rub your palms together until they feel warm. Then stroke firmly from the fingers of one hand up over the wrist.
steps.sensationCue: Warmth spreading through cold, stiff fingers.
steps.rhythm: One long stroke every two seconds
steps.breathCue: Slow breath out as you stroke
steps.voiceScript: Rub your palms together briskly until they feel warm. Then wrap one hand around the other and stroke firmly from the fingers up over the wrist, a few times each side.

steps.title: Circle your wrists slowly
steps.body: Let your hands hang loose and circle both wrists five times each way. Keep the circles slow and easy.
steps.sensationCue: Smooth, quiet movement. No clicks or catching.
steps.rhythm: One circle every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out through the slow part
steps.voiceScript: Let your hands hang loose from the wrists. Circle them slowly five times one way, then five times back, and keep your fingers soft the whole time.
steps.commonMistake: Do not force a big circle. Go as far as feels easy, no further.

steps.title: Press your palm open
steps.body: Put both thumbs in the middle of your palm. Draw them slowly apart to open the hand, then start again a little lower.
steps.sensationCue: A broad, spreading stretch across the palm.
steps.rhythm: One slow spread every five seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you spread
steps.voiceScript: Turn one palm up and place both thumbs together in the middle of it, fingers wrapped around the back. Draw your thumbs slowly apart so the palm opens out. Work up and down the hand, then swap.
steps.commonMistake: Do not dig into one point. Spread wide and slow instead.

steps.title: Work the base of your thumb
steps.body: Find the fleshy mound at the base of your thumb. Make small, slow circles into it with your other thumb.
steps.sensationCue: A deep, dull ache right where the mouse sits. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: About one small circle per second
steps.breathCue: Breathe out into the sore spots
steps.voiceScript: Find the fleshy mound at the base of your thumb, the part that does all the gripping and scrolling. Press your other thumb into it and make small, slow circles over the whole mound. Give it about twenty seconds each hand.
steps.commonMistake: Do not squeeze the whole hand. Aim for that one fleshy mound.
steps.caution: Ease off if you get pins and needles in your fingers.

steps.title: Slide between the hand bones
steps.body: Turn your hand palm down. Slide your thumb along each groove between the long bones, from the knuckles back to the wrist.
steps.sensationCue: Narrow lines of tenderness that ease as you pass.
steps.rhythm: One slow slide per groove
steps.breathCue: Steady, unhurried breathing
steps.voiceScript: Turn one hand palm down and feel the grooves between the long bones on the back of it. Slide your other thumb slowly along each groove, from the knuckle back towards the wrist. Four grooves on each hand.
steps.commonMistake: Do not press on the bones. Stay in the soft grooves between them.

steps.title: Squeeze your forearm
steps.body: Wrap your hand around the meat of the opposite forearm, just below the elbow. Squeeze and release your way down to the wrist.
steps.sensationCue: Tight ropes of muscle softening under the squeeze.
steps.rhythm: One squeeze per second, moving as you go
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you squeeze
steps.voiceScript: Wrap your hand around the fleshy top of the opposite forearm, just below the elbow. Squeeze, let go, and work your way down to the wrist. Do the top of the forearm and the underside, then swap arms.
steps.commonMistake: Do not skip this. Most typing ache starts in the forearm, not the hand.

steps.title: Pull and circle each finger
steps.body: Take each finger in turn. Pull gently for two seconds, then circle it once each way.
steps.sensationCue: A small release in every knuckle. Never a wrench.
steps.rhythm: About three seconds per finger
steps.breathCue: Easy breaths, shoulders down
steps.voiceScript: Take each finger between your thumb and finger, one at a time. Pull gently for a couple of seconds, then circle it once each way. Work through all five, then swap hands.
steps.commonMistake: Do not pull for a crack. A steady, gentle pull is plenty.

steps.title: Stretch and shake out
steps.body: Press your palms together in front of your chest and lower them until you feel a stretch. Hold, then shake your hands out loose.
steps.sensationCue: A gentle pull through the wrist. Nothing pinching in front.
steps.rhythm: Hold fifteen seconds, then shake for ten
steps.breathCue: Long breath out while you hold
steps.voiceScript: Press your palms together in front of your chest, fingers pointing up. Lower your hands slowly until you feel a gentle pull through the wrists, and hold there for fifteen seconds. Then let go and shake your hands out loose.
steps.caution: Stop the stretch if it pinches in the front of the wrist.

steps.title: Rest your palms and settle
steps.body: Lie on your back and rest both palms on your forehead. Take three slow breaths and let your head get heavy in the pillow.
steps.sensationCue: Warmth on the forehead. The pillow taking your weight.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: Long, slow breath out through your nose
steps.voiceScript: Lie on your back with a pillow under your head and rest both palms across your forehead. Do not move at all. Take three slow breaths and let your head get heavier in the pillow with each one.
steps.commonMistake: Do not start rubbing straight away. The stillness sets everything up.

steps.title: Smooth your forehead
steps.body: Draw your fingertips from the middle of your brow out to the temples. Lift off, start a little higher, and work up to the hairline.
steps.sensationCue: The frown letting go. Smooth and unhurried.
steps.rhythm: One slow sweep every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out along each sweep
steps.voiceScript: Bring your fingertips to the middle of your brow, just above your nose. Draw them out towards your temples, lift off, and start again a little higher. Keep going until you have covered the whole forehead up to the hairline.

steps.title: Circle along your hairline
steps.body: Set your fingertips at your hairline and make small circles. Move the skin over the bone rather than sliding across it.
steps.sensationCue: The scalp shifting in one piece. No scratching.
steps.rhythm: Three or four circles, then move a finger-width
steps.breathCue: Quiet, even breathing
steps.voiceScript: Put your fingertips along your hairline and make small circles there. The trick is to move the skin over the bone rather than sliding your fingers across the skin. Work slowly from the middle out towards each temple.
steps.commonMistake: Do not scratch with your nails. Move the skin, not your fingers.

steps.title: Shampoo circles all over
steps.body: Spread your fingers and work all over your scalp, like washing your hair without water. Cover the top, the sides and the back.
steps.sensationCue: A tingling, loosening feeling spreading over your head.
steps.rhythm: Slow circles, moving on every few seconds
steps.breathCue: Keep your breathing long and quiet
steps.voiceScript: Spread your fingers and work them all over your scalp, like you are washing your hair without any water. Take your time over the sides above your ears, then the top, then as much of the back as you can reach against the pillow.
steps.commonMistake: Do not only work the top. The sides above your ears hold the most.

steps.title: Lift and release your hair
steps.body: Take a small handful of hair close to the roots. Lift until you feel a gentle pull, hold two seconds, then let go.
steps.sensationCue: A pleasant tug at the roots. Never enough to sting.
steps.rhythm: Lift, hold two seconds, release, move on
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you let go
steps.voiceScript: Gather a small handful of hair close to the roots. Lift it straight up until you feel a gentle pull across the scalp, hold for two seconds, and let it go. Move around your head a handful at a time.
steps.commonMistake: Do not grab the ends. Hold close to the scalp so nothing tugs.
steps.caution: Skip this one if your hair is fine, fragile or thinning.

steps.title: Press under your skull
steps.body: Slide your fingertips under the bony ridge at the back of your head. Let the weight of your head press into them and hold.
steps.sensationCue: A slow melt that spreads up into your head.
steps.rhythm: Hold twenty seconds, then move a thumb-width outward
steps.breathCue: Long breath out as you sink in
steps.voiceScript: Slide your fingertips under the bony ridge at the back of your head, either side of the middle. Now stop pushing and simply let the weight of your head rest down onto them. Hold for twenty seconds, then move your fingers out a little towards your ears.
steps.commonMistake: Do not lift your head to help. Let the pillow and your hands do it.
steps.caution: Stay either side of the bony spine, never on it.

steps.title: Circle your temples slowly
steps.body: Put two fingers on each temple, just above the ear. Make circles so slow you could count each one.
steps.sensationCue: Pressure easing behind the eyes. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: One circle every two seconds
steps.breathCue: Slower out than in
steps.voiceScript: Rest two fingers on each temple, just above and in front of the ear. Circle them so slowly that you could count each turn. Let your elbows be heavy and your jaw soft while you do it.
steps.commonMistake: Do not press hard here. The temple is thin and likes light work.

steps.title: Cup your palms over your eyes
steps.body: Cup both palms over your closed eyes so no weight lands on them. Rest in that darkness for a slow count of thirty.
steps.sensationCue: Warm darkness. No weight at all on the eyes.
steps.rhythm: Still
steps.breathCue: Breathe out longer than you breathe in
steps.voiceScript: Close your eyes and cup both palms over them, so the edges of your hands rest on the bone and nothing touches the eyes themselves. Stay in that warm darkness for a slow count of thirty, and let your breathing get longer.
steps.caution: Rest your hands on the bone around the eyes. Never press on the eyeball.

steps.title: Let your hands drift down
steps.body: Let your arms slide down onto the bed and stop moving. Stay still and let your breathing get slower and slower.
steps.sensationCue: Heaviness, quiet, nothing left to do.
steps.rhythm: No movement at all
steps.breathCue: Slow, quiet breaths — let them fade
steps.voiceScript: Let your arms slide down onto the bed and leave them wherever they land. There is nothing left to do now. Let your breathing get slower, and let yourself drift off whenever you are ready.
steps.commonMistake: Do not do one more bit. Stopping is the last step.

steps.title: Open the hollows above your collarbone
steps.body: Rest your fingertips in the soft hollows just above your collarbones. Press in feather-light and release, like a slow pump, twenty times.
steps.sensationCue: Barely-there pressure. Skin moves, muscle does not.
steps.rhythm: One gentle pump every two seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out on each press
steps.voiceScript: Cross your hands and rest your fingertips in the soft hollows just above your collarbones. Press in as lightly as if you were pressing on a soap bubble, then release. Twenty slow pumps, and no more pressure than that.
steps.commonMistake: Do not push deep. This work sits just under the skin.
steps.caution: Feather-light only, and stay well off the front of your throat.

steps.title: Sweep down your neck
steps.body: Lay flat fingers just below your ears. Stroke slowly down the sides of your neck to your collarbones, ten times each side.
steps.sensationCue: A light drag on the skin. Nothing pressing inward.
steps.rhythm: One slow sweep every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Long breath out down each sweep
steps.voiceScript: Lay flat fingers on the sides of your neck, just below your ears. Stroke slowly downward to the collarbones, so lightly that the skin barely moves ahead of your hand. Ten passes each side, and always downward.
steps.commonMistake: Do not work upward. Everything drains downward from here.
steps.caution: Keep to the soft sides of the neck. Never press the front of your throat.

steps.title: Pump in front of your ears
steps.body: Place two fingers in the small dip just in front of each ear. Press in lightly and release, twenty slow pumps.
steps.sensationCue: A soft, hollow feeling. No dragging on the skin.
steps.rhythm: One pump every two seconds
steps.breathCue: Quiet, even breathing
steps.voiceScript: Find the small dip just in front of each ear, level with your cheekbone. Rest two fingers there and press in very lightly, then release, twenty times. This is the doorway everything else will be swept towards.

steps.title: Drain your jawline to your ears
steps.body: Set flat fingers either side of your chin. Glide them along your jawline out to your ears, then lift off and start again.
steps.sensationCue: A light, gliding sweep. Never a drag or a pull.
steps.rhythm: One glide every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Slow breath out with each sweep
steps.voiceScript: Set flat fingers either side of your chin, one hand for each side of the jaw. Glide them along the jawline out towards your ears, finishing in that dip you just pumped. Lift off, go back to the chin, and repeat about ten times.
steps.commonMistake: Do not stop halfway. Always finish the sweep at the ear.

steps.title: Sweep your cheeks toward your ears
steps.body: Lay flat fingers beside your nose. Sweep out across your cheeks to your ears, so light that the skin barely moves ahead of you.
steps.sensationCue: Almost nothing — a whisper of movement. Never a rub.
steps.rhythm: One sweep every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out along each sweep
steps.voiceScript: Lay flat fingers on your cheeks, either side of your nose. Sweep them outward towards your ears, keeping the touch so light it is almost nothing. Work the upper cheek, then the middle, then along the top of the jaw.
steps.commonMistake: Do not press into the cheek. Light and wide beats deep and small.

steps.title: Trace under your eyes
steps.body: Use your ring finger to trace the bone under each eye, from the inner corner out to the temple. Repeat ten times.
steps.sensationCue: Feather-light along the bone. No pull on the eyelid.
steps.rhythm: One slow trace every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Soft, quiet breaths
steps.voiceScript: Use your ring finger, because it presses the least. Trace the bone under each eye, starting at the inner corner and travelling out to the temple, then carry on down in front of the ear. Ten light passes.
steps.commonMistake: Do not stretch the skin. The skin here is the thinnest on your body.
steps.caution: Stay on the bony rim under the eye. Never press on the eyeball itself.

steps.title: Smooth your brows outward
steps.body: Run your thumbs along the ridge under your eyebrows, from the inner ends out to the temples. Finish each pass at the hairline.
steps.sensationCue: A pleasant firm line along the brow bone. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: One slow pass every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you smooth
steps.voiceScript: Rest your thumbs under the inner ends of your eyebrows, on the bony ridge. Run them outward along the brow bone to the temples, and finish each pass by dropping down in front of the ear. Repeat about ten times.
steps.caution: Work on the bone above the eye socket, never down into the eye.

steps.title: Fan across your forehead
steps.body: Start between your brows and fan your fingertips out to the temples. Work up the forehead line by line until you reach the hairline.
steps.sensationCue: The forehead unclenching. Light, wide, unhurried.
steps.rhythm: One fan every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Long, quiet breaths
steps.voiceScript: Start with your fingertips between your brows. Fan them outward to the temples, lift off, and begin again a little higher up the forehead. Every stroke heads out towards the ears, never side to side.
steps.commonMistake: Do not scrub side to side. Every stroke heads out toward the ears.

steps.title: Empty everything down your neck
steps.body: From behind your ears, stroke down the sides of your neck to the hollows above your collarbones. Twenty slow passes, each lighter than the last.
steps.sensationCue: A downward, emptying feeling. Nothing pressing in.
steps.rhythm: One long stroke every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out along the whole stroke
steps.voiceScript: Everything you have moved forward now needs somewhere to go. Start behind your ears and stroke down the sides of your neck to the hollows above your collarbones, twenty slow times. Make each pass a little lighter than the one before.
steps.caution: Soft sides of the neck only. Never the front of the throat.

steps.title: Rest your palms on your face
steps.body: Cup both palms over your face without pressing. Breathe into your hands three times, then let them fall into your lap.
steps.sensationCue: Warm, still, and lighter around the eyes.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: Three slow breaths into your palms
steps.voiceScript: Cup both palms over your face, resting them so gently that nothing presses in. Breathe into your hands three times. Then let your hands fall into your lap and open your eyes slowly.

steps.title: Warm your cheeks and jaw
steps.body: Lay both palms flat over your cheeks. Make slow, wide circles over the whole jaw, letting the skin move with your hands.
steps.sensationCue: Warmth spreading through the cheeks. Nothing sharp.
steps.rhythm: One slow circle every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Slow breath out with each circle
steps.voiceScript: Lay both palms flat over your cheeks, fingers pointing up towards your temples. Make slow, wide circles over the whole jaw and cheek, letting the skin move with your hands rather than sliding across it.

steps.title: Let your jaw hang loose
steps.body: Rest the tip of your tongue behind your top teeth and let your teeth come apart. Sit like that for a slow count of thirty.
steps.sensationCue: The jaw dropping open by itself. No effort at all.
steps.rhythm: Still — just breathing
steps.breathCue: In and out through your nose
steps.voiceScript: Rest the tip of your tongue lightly behind your top teeth and let your back teeth come apart. Lips together, teeth apart. Sit there for a slow count of thirty and notice how much work you were doing without knowing it.
steps.commonMistake: Do not force your mouth open. Just stop holding it shut.

steps.title: Circle the muscle in your cheek
steps.body: Clench once to feel the pad of muscle above your back teeth, then let go. Make slow circles there with two fingertips.
steps.sensationCue: A deep, dull ache that softens as you work. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: About one small circle per second
steps.breathCue: Breathe out and let your jaw go soft
steps.voiceScript: Clench your teeth once and feel the pad of muscle bulge in your cheek, above the back teeth. Now unclench and keep your fingers where that bulge was. Make slow circles there, working both sides at once, and keep the jaw loose while you do it.
steps.commonMistake: Do not work with your teeth clenched. Find the muscle, then let go.

steps.title: Hold the sore spot
steps.body: Find the tenderest point in that muscle and press straight in. Hold still for twenty seconds each side, then ease off slowly.
steps.sensationCue: A strong ache that fades by about half while you hold.
steps.rhythm: Still — hold, do not rub
steps.breathCue: Long breath out into the hold
steps.voiceScript: Search that cheek muscle for the single most tender point, usually about a finger-width in front of your ear lobe. Press straight in with your thumb and hold, without rubbing, for twenty seconds. Ease off slowly, then do the other side.
steps.commonMistake: Do not hunt for more pain. One clear spot per side is plenty.
steps.caution: Gentle pressure only. Stop if you get pain in the ear, the teeth or the joint.

steps.title: Fan out over your temples
steps.body: Put two fingers on each temple. Circle slowly and work outward and upward in a fan, following the muscle above your ear.
steps.sensationCue: A dull tightness easing above the ear. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: One circle every two seconds
steps.breathCue: Quiet, easy breathing
steps.voiceScript: Rest two fingers on each temple. Circle slowly, then fan outward and upward, following that broad chewing muscle in an arc above and behind your ear. Clench once and you will feel exactly where it runs.
steps.commonMistake: Do not press hard on the temple. Light circles do more here.

steps.title: Work inside your cheek
steps.body: With a clean hand, put your thumb inside your cheek and your fingers outside. Gently squeeze the firm band of muscle and hold ten seconds.
steps.sensationCue: A strong but bearable ache in one small band. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: Hold ten seconds, release, move a little
steps.breathCue: Breathe through your nose and stay loose
steps.voiceScript: Wash your hands first and check your nails are short. Slide your thumb inside your cheek, along the outer edge beside your back teeth, with your fingers on the outside. Squeeze that firm band gently between them, hold for ten seconds, then move a little and repeat.
steps.commonMistake: Do not pinch the soft inner cheek. Aim for the firm band of muscle.
steps.caution: Wash your hands and keep nails short. Stay off the gums, and stop if it hurts.

steps.title: Open and close slowly
steps.body: Rest your tongue on the roof of your mouth and open your mouth slowly, then close it. Keep it small and straight, ten times.
steps.sensationCue: A smooth, even track. No clicking or sliding sideways.
steps.rhythm: One slow open and close every four seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you open
steps.voiceScript: Rest your tongue on the roof of your mouth and open your jaw slowly, only as far as the tongue stays put. Close just as slowly. Ten small, straight openings, watching that your chin does not drift to one side.
steps.commonMistake: Do not open as wide as you can. Small and smooth is the point.
steps.caution: Stop if your jaw clicks, catches or locks, and get it looked at.

steps.title: Rest your palms and finish
steps.body: Rest both palms over your jaw with no pressure at all. Take three slow breaths, then let your hands fall away.
steps.sensationCue: Warm, still, teeth apart and heavy.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: Three long breaths out
steps.voiceScript: Rest both palms over your jaw, warm and still, with no pressure at all. Take three slow breaths and let your teeth stay apart. Then let your hands fall into your lap.
steps.commonMistake: Do not go straight back to clenching. Keep your teeth apart.

steps.title: Cup your hands over your eyes
steps.body: Rub your palms together until they feel warm. Cup them over your closed eyes without touching them, and breathe.
steps.sensationCue: Warm and dark. No pressure at all on the eyes.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: Three slow breaths out
steps.voiceScript: Rub your palms together for a few seconds until they feel warm. Now cup them over your closed eyes, resting the edges of your hands on your cheekbones so nothing presses on the eyes themselves. Take three slow breaths in the dark.
steps.commonMistake: Do not press on your eyes. The heels of your hands rest on bone.
steps.caution: Never put pressure on the eyeball itself.

steps.title: Warm your forehead with flat fingers
steps.body: Lay three fingers of each hand in the middle of your forehead. Sweep them out to your temples, slow and light.
steps.sensationCue: Smooth and warm. The skin should glide, never drag.
steps.rhythm: One sweep every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out on every sweep
steps.voiceScript: Lay three fingers of each hand flat in the middle of your forehead. Sweep them outward to your temples, slowly and lightly, then lift off and start again. Let your face soften as you go.
steps.commonMistake: Do not drag on dry skin. Keep it light enough to glide.

steps.title: Circle your temples
steps.body: Put two fingertips on each temple, in the soft dip beside your eyebrow. Circle slowly, moving the skin instead of sliding over it.
steps.sensationCue: A dull, satisfying ache that eases as you circle. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: One slow circle per second
steps.breathCue: Long breath out through your nose
steps.voiceScript: Find the soft dip on each temple, just beside the outer end of your eyebrow. Rest two fingertips there and make slow circles, moving the skin with you instead of sliding across it. Clench your teeth once and you will feel the muscle move under your fingers.
steps.commonMistake: Do not press hard here. The bone is thin and the muscle is small.

steps.title: Press along your brow line
steps.body: Pinch the ridge of your eyebrow between thumb and finger at the inner corner. Hold three seconds, move out a little, and repeat.
steps.sensationCue: A bright, sore pinch that fades fast. Never a stab.
steps.rhythm: Three seconds on, then move out
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you squeeze
steps.voiceScript: Take the ridge of your eyebrow between your thumb and first finger, starting at the inner corner near your nose. Squeeze gently for three seconds, let go, and move out a finger width. Work all the way to the outer end, then do the other side.
steps.commonMistake: Do not slide down onto the eyelid. Stay on the bony ridge.
steps.caution: Stay on the brow bone. Never press on the eye itself.

steps.title: Press the points beside your nose
steps.body: Put a fingertip either side of your nose, level with the nostrils, in the small dip against the cheekbone. Press in and up.
steps.sensationCue: A full, achy pressure that can make your nose run. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: Ten seconds on, five seconds off
steps.breathCue: Breathe out slowly through your mouth
steps.voiceScript: Find the small dip either side of your nose, level with your nostrils, where the cheekbone begins. Press in and slightly upward with a fingertip on each side and hold for ten seconds. Ease off, breathe, then do it again.
steps.commonMistake: Do not press into the nostril. Aim for the bone at the edge.
steps.caution: Skip this if the skin over your sinuses is hot, swollen or very tender.

steps.title: Sweep under your cheekbones
steps.body: Rest your fingertips beside your nose again. Sweep out under the cheekbone towards your ear, then down the side of your neck.
steps.sensationCue: Light and drifting, barely more than skin deep. Never firm.
steps.rhythm: One slow sweep every four seconds
steps.breathCue: Steady, easy breathing
steps.voiceScript: Start with your fingertips beside your nose and sweep outward under the cheekbone, all the way to the front of your ear. Then carry on down the side of your neck towards the collarbone. Keep it feather light, because this one works on the surface.
steps.commonMistake: Heavy pressure does nothing here. Lighter is better.

steps.title: Work the base of your skull
steps.body: Curl your fingertips under the bony ridge at the back of your head. Make small circles either side of the middle, letting your head get heavy.
steps.sensationCue: A melting release that spreads up over your scalp. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: Four circles, then move a thumb-width
steps.breathCue: Let your head rest into your fingers
steps.voiceScript: Curl your fingertips up under the bony ridge at the back of your head, where the skull meets the neck. Let the weight of your head rest into them and make small, slow circles. Work outward towards your ears a thumb width at a time.
steps.commonMistake: Do not dig with your nails. Use the soft pads of your fingers.
steps.caution: Stay either side of the bony bumps of the spine, never on them.

steps.title: Squeeze the web of your hand
steps.body: Pinch the fleshy web between your thumb and index finger. Squeeze towards the bone of the index finger and hold, then swap hands.
steps.sensationCue: A strong, spreading ache. Often sorer on one hand than the other.
steps.rhythm: Thirty seconds on each hand
steps.breathCue: Breathe out into the squeeze
steps.voiceScript: Take the fleshy web between your thumb and index finger and squeeze it, angling the pressure towards the bone of the index finger. Hold for thirty slow seconds, breathing out into it, then swap hands.
steps.commonMistake: Do not rub it. Steady pressure works better than movement.
steps.caution: Skip this point completely if you are pregnant.

steps.title: Palm your eyes and rest
steps.body: Warm your palms again and cup them over your closed eyes. Sit still and let your face and jaw go loose.
steps.sensationCue: Quiet, warm and dark. Your jaw should unclench.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: Four slow breaths out
steps.voiceScript: Rub your palms warm one more time and cup them over your closed eyes. Let your jaw hang loose and your shoulders drop. Stay here for four slow breaths, then take your hands away gently and open your eyes.

steps.title: Open and close your hands
steps.body: Spread your fingers as wide as they go, then curl them into a loose fist. Repeat slowly, then circle each wrist a few times.
steps.sensationCue: Stiff at first, easier by the tenth one. Never painful.
steps.rhythm: One open and close every two seconds
steps.breathCue: Easy, steady breathing
steps.voiceScript: Spread your fingers as wide as they will go, hold for a second, then curl them into a loose fist. Repeat that ten times, and finish with a few slow circles of each wrist. This wakes everything up before you press on it.
steps.commonMistake: Do not squeeze the fist hard. Loose is the point.

steps.title: Warm the whole forearm
steps.body: Rest one arm on the desk, palm up. Stroke firmly from wrist to elbow with your other palm, then turn the arm over and repeat.
steps.sensationCue: Warm and smooth, like ironing. Nothing sharp.
steps.rhythm: One long stroke every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Slow breath out on each stroke
steps.voiceScript: Rest one forearm on the desk with the palm facing up. Using the flat of your other hand, stroke firmly from the wrist up towards the elbow, then lift off and start again. After twenty seconds, turn the arm over and warm the top the same way.
steps.commonMistake: Do not stroke back down. Work towards the elbow each time.

steps.title: Knead the soft inner forearm
steps.body: Turn your arm palm up. Squeeze the meaty muscle below the elbow between thumb and fingers, working slowly down towards the wrist.
steps.sensationCue: A deep, dull ache that softens as you work. Never sharp or tingly.
steps.rhythm: One squeeze per second, moving down
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you squeeze
steps.voiceScript: With your arm palm up on the desk, take the meaty muscle just below the elbow between your thumb and fingers. Squeeze, let go, and creep a little further down the arm. Stop about two finger widths above the wrist crease.
steps.commonMistake: Do not carry on into the wrist. That is where the nerve runs.
steps.caution: Stay off the middle of the wrist crease. Never press hard there.

steps.title: Thumb walk down the top
steps.body: Turn your arm palm down. Press your thumb into the muscle on top of the forearm and walk slowly from below the elbow to the wrist.
steps.sensationCue: Firm and achy, often more tender than you expect. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: Press two seconds, move a thumb-width
steps.breathCue: Steady breathing, no holding
steps.voiceScript: Turn your arm palm down on the desk. Sink your thumb into the muscle on top of the forearm, hold for two seconds, then move a thumb width towards the wrist. This band does most of the work when you use a mouse, so take your time.
steps.commonMistake: Do not use your thumb tip. Press with the flat pad.

steps.title: Hold the sore outer elbow spot
steps.body: With the arm palm down, feel two finger widths below the outside of the elbow. Press into the tender knot there and hold still.
steps.sensationCue: A strong ache that may spread down the arm. Never electric.
steps.rhythm: Hold twenty seconds, then ease off
steps.breathCue: Breathe out into the pressure
steps.voiceScript: Keep the arm palm down and feel about two finger widths below the outside of the elbow. There is usually a tender knot there in anyone who uses a keyboard. Press into it with your thumb and hold, still and steady, for twenty seconds.
steps.commonMistake: Do not rub the spot. Still pressure is what lets it let go.
steps.caution: If the ache turns to burning, or you feel tingling in your fingers, come off it.

steps.title: Circle below the inner elbow
steps.body: Turn palm up and find the muscle just below the inner elbow. Make small circles there, staying off the bony knob of the funny bone.
steps.sensationCue: Achy and firm. Any zing into the little finger means move.
steps.rhythm: Slow circles, moving a little each time
steps.breathCue: Long, slow breath out
steps.voiceScript: Turn the arm palm up and find the soft muscle just below the crease of your inner elbow. Make small, slow circles into it with your fingertips. Keep well away from the bony knob on the inside, the funny bone, because a nerve sits right on it.
steps.commonMistake: Do not press the bony knob. The nerve there does not like it.
steps.caution: Never press directly on the funny bone. Tingling means move off.

steps.title: Stretch the front of your wrist
steps.body: Straighten one arm, palm forward like a stop sign. Use your other hand to draw the fingers gently back, and hold.
steps.sensationCue: A long pull down the inside of the forearm. Never a pinch at the wrist.
steps.rhythm: Twenty seconds on each side
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as the stretch eases
steps.voiceScript: Straighten one arm in front of you, palm facing away like a stop sign. With your other hand, draw the fingers gently back towards you until you feel a long pull down the inside of the forearm. Hold for twenty slow seconds, then swap arms.
steps.commonMistake: Do not lock the elbow hard. Keep a soft bend.

steps.title: Stretch the back and shake out
steps.body: Point your fingers down with the palm facing you and press the back of the hand gently. Then drop your arms and shake both hands loose.
steps.sensationCue: A pull along the top of the forearm, then loose, warm hands.
steps.rhythm: Fifteen seconds each side, then shake
steps.breathCue: Sigh out on the shake
steps.voiceScript: Now turn the hand the other way, fingers pointing down and the palm facing you, and press gently on the back of the hand until the top of the forearm pulls. Fifteen seconds each side. Then let your arms hang and shake both hands out, like you are flicking off water.

steps.title: Rock your hips against the wall
steps.body: Stand with your back to the wall, knees soft. Tuck your tailbone under so your lower back flattens, then let it curve back.
steps.sensationCue: A gentle rocking through the lower back. Never a pinch.
steps.rhythm: One slow rock every four seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you flatten
steps.voiceScript: Stand with your back against the wall and your knees slightly bent. Tuck your tailbone under so the small of your back flattens into the wall, then let it curve away again. Keep it slow and small, this is only to wake the area up.
steps.commonMistake: Do not force the movement. Small and slow is enough.

steps.title: Warm your lower back with knuckles
steps.body: Make loose fists and rest the flat of your knuckles either side of your spine. Rub briskly up and down until the skin feels warm.
steps.sensationCue: Warm and buzzy, like standing near a fire. Never sore.
steps.rhythm: Brisk — about two rubs per second
steps.breathCue: Easy, steady breathing
steps.voiceScript: Make loose fists and put the flat of your knuckles on the muscle either side of your spine, just above your belt line. Rub briskly up and down for about half a minute, until the skin under your hands feels properly warm.
steps.commonMistake: Do not rub on the bumps of the spine. Stay on the muscle either side.
steps.caution: Keep your knuckles off the spine itself.

steps.title: Roll the ball against the wall
steps.body: Trap a tennis ball between the wall and the muscle beside your spine. Bend and straighten your knees to roll it slowly up and down.
steps.sensationCue: Firm pressure you control by leaning. A good ache, never sharp.
steps.rhythm: One slow pass every ten seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you lean in
steps.voiceScript: Put the tennis ball between the wall and the muscle running alongside your spine, about a hand's width above your belt. Bend your knees to slide down, then straighten to come back up, rolling the ball slowly over the muscle. Do about thirty seconds on each side.
steps.commonMistake: Do not roll fast. Slow finds more than hard does.
steps.caution: Never let the ball sit on your spine. Stay on the muscle beside it.

steps.title: Lean into the sorest spot
steps.body: When the ball finds a spot that complains, stop there. Lean your weight in and hold still while you take five slow breaths.
steps.sensationCue: A strong ache that fades by about half while you hold.
steps.rhythm: Hold thirty seconds on each spot
steps.breathCue: Breathe out long into the ball
steps.voiceScript: When the ball rolls over somewhere that really complains, stop and stay there. Lean your weight into the wall and hold, taking five slow breaths, and let the muscle give way under it. Step your feet away from the wall a little if you want less pressure.
steps.commonMistake: Do not hold your breath. Breathing out is what softens it.
steps.caution: If the pressure sends a sharp line down your leg, move off that spot.

steps.title: Work the top of your hip
steps.body: Drop the ball to just above the rim of your hip bone, off to the side. Roll small and slow along that shelf of muscle.
steps.sensationCue: Tender and thick, like a rope under the ball. Never bony pain.
steps.rhythm: Small rolls, pausing where it bites
steps.breathCue: Long breath out on each pause
steps.voiceScript: Slide the ball down and out until it sits just above the rim of your hip bone, off to the side of your back. Roll it in small, slow circles along that shelf of muscle. It is often the most tender part of the whole routine, so lean in gently.
steps.commonMistake: Do not roll onto the hip bone. Stay on the muscle above it.

steps.title: Take the ball to the floor
steps.body: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat. Slide the ball under one side of your lower back and let your weight sink onto it.
steps.sensationCue: Deeper than the wall, because your own weight does the work.
steps.rhythm: Sink for twenty seconds, shift, repeat
steps.breathCue: Breathe out and let your weight drop
steps.voiceScript: Lie down on a mat with your knees bent and your feet flat. Slide the ball under one side of your lower back, beside the spine, and let your weight settle onto it for about twenty seconds. Lift your hips a little to move it, then settle again.
steps.commonMistake: Do not flop down onto it. Lower yourself slowly with your hands.
steps.caution: Keep the ball beside the spine, never under the bones of the spine.

steps.title: Roll the top of your buttock
steps.body: Move the ball down onto the muscle at the top of your buttock. Let that knee fall out to the side to sink in deeper.
steps.sensationCue: A broad, deep ache. Never a sharp line down the leg.
steps.rhythm: Twenty seconds per spot, three spots
steps.breathCue: Breathe out and let the hip soften
steps.voiceScript: Move the ball down onto the thick muscle at the top of your buttock, out from the tailbone. Let that knee fall open to the side to sink deeper, and hold for twenty seconds before shifting to a new spot.
steps.commonMistake: Do not sit on the tailbone itself. Stay out on the muscle.
steps.caution: Stay off the bony tailbone and the flat plate of bone beside it.

steps.title: Hug your knees and rock
steps.body: Take the ball out. Draw both knees up to your chest, hold your shins, and rock gently from side to side.
steps.sensationCue: A long, easy stretch across the lower back. Never a pinch.
steps.rhythm: One slow rock every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you rock
steps.voiceScript: Take the ball out and draw both knees up towards your chest. Hold your shins and rock gently from side to side, letting the floor rub your lower back for you. Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the mat.
steps.commonMistake: Do not pull hard on your knees. Let your arms be lazy.

steps.title: Lie flat and breathe
steps.body: Put your feet flat and your hands on your belly. Breathe so your belly rises, and feel your back settle into the floor.
steps.sensationCue: Wide, heavy and still. The floor should feel like it holds you.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: In for four, out for six
steps.voiceScript: Let your feet come flat to the floor and rest both hands on your belly. Breathe in so your belly lifts your hands, then let the air out slowly. Stay for about a minute and feel your back spread out on the mat.

steps.title: Sit tall and rock your hips
steps.body: Sit on a firm chair with both feet flat. Rock slowly forward and back on your sitting bones, then stop in the middle.
steps.sensationCue: Easy movement through the hips. Nothing should pinch.
steps.rhythm: One slow rock every four seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you settle
steps.voiceScript: Sit on a firm chair with both feet flat on the floor. Rock slowly forwards and backwards on your sitting bones, then stop in the middle, where you feel tall and balanced. Take a couple of easy breaths there.
steps.commonMistake: Do not perch on the front edge. Sit with your whole weight down.

steps.title: Warm the muscle with your fist
steps.body: Lean onto one hip and rub the meat of the other buttock with a loose fist. Big, firm circles until it feels warm.
steps.sensationCue: Warm and broad. Nothing pointy or sharp.
steps.rhythm: About one circle per second
steps.breathCue: Steady, easy breathing
steps.voiceScript: Lean your weight onto one hip and make a loose fist. Rub big, firm circles into the meat of the other buttock until it feels warm, then lean the other way and do the second side. Twenty seconds each is plenty.
steps.commonMistake: Do not use your knuckle points. Use the flat of your fist.

steps.title: Sit on the ball
steps.body: Put the ball under one buttock, out from the middle. Sit down slowly and hunt around until you find the spot that talks back.
steps.sensationCue: A deep, dull ache in one small place. Never sharp or electric.
steps.rhythm: Shift a little every ten seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you sink
steps.voiceScript: Put the ball on the chair and lower yourself onto it so it sits under the meaty part of one buttock, out from the middle. Shift around slowly until you find the spot that really talks back. Take some weight on your hands and feet if you want less pressure.
steps.commonMistake: Do not drop your full weight on straight away. Ease down.
steps.caution: Keep the ball off the tailbone and off the sitting bone. Muscle only.

steps.title: Cross your ankle and sink
steps.body: Rest the ankle of the ball side on your opposite knee. That opens the deep hip muscle, so let your weight settle in and hold.
steps.sensationCue: The ache gets deeper and more exact. Never a zing down the leg.
steps.rhythm: Hold thirty seconds, then ease off
steps.breathCue: Long breath out into the ball
steps.voiceScript: Lift the foot on the ball side and rest that ankle on your opposite knee, letting the knee fall open. That opens up the deep muscle under the ball. Let your weight settle and hold for thirty slow seconds.
steps.commonMistake: Do not push the open knee down with your hand. Let it hang.
steps.caution: A sharp or electric feeling down the back of the leg means move the ball. That is nerve, not muscle.

steps.title: Rock slowly over the spot
steps.body: Keep the ankle crossed and rock a small amount side to side. Let the ball roll across the muscle rather than along it.
steps.sensationCue: A rolling ache that moves as you rock. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: One slow rock every four seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out on each pass
steps.voiceScript: Keep that ankle crossed and rock a short distance from side to side, so the ball rolls across the muscle rather than along it. Small movements are enough. If a spot really bites, stop there and breathe until it eases.
steps.commonMistake: Do not go hunting for the worst pain. Strong but bearable is right.

steps.title: Find the deep hip knot
steps.body: Move the ball out towards the side of your hip, halfway between the tailbone and the bony point. Sink in and hold still.
steps.sensationCue: A wide ache that spreads through the buttock. Never down the leg.
steps.rhythm: Hold thirty seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out and let the hip drop
steps.voiceScript: Move the ball outwards so it sits about halfway between your tailbone and the bony point at the side of your hip. That is where the deep hip muscle lies. Sink onto it and hold still for thirty seconds, breathing out slowly.
steps.commonMistake: Do not rub back and forth. Stillness is what softens a knot.
steps.caution: Come off it at once if you feel tingling or numbness in the leg.

steps.title: Swap sides and repeat
steps.body: Lift off, move the ball under the other buttock, and work through the same three positions. Give this side the same time.
steps.sensationCue: Often more tender than the first side. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: Twenty seconds in each position
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you sink
steps.voiceScript: Lift your weight off and slide the ball under the other buttock. Work through the same three positions: sitting straight, then ankle crossed, then out towards the side of the hip. Give this side the same time even if it feels easier.
steps.commonMistake: Do not skip the easy side. Hips like to be even.

steps.title: Sit into a figure four
steps.body: Take the ball away. Cross one ankle over the opposite knee and lean your chest forward, keeping your back long.
steps.sensationCue: A broad stretch deep in the buttock. Never a pinch at the front of the hip.
steps.rhythm: Thirty seconds on each side
steps.breathCue: Breathe out and lean a little further
steps.voiceScript: Take the ball away and sit tall. Cross one ankle over the opposite knee, then hinge your chest forward, keeping your back long. Hold for thirty seconds where you feel a broad stretch deep in the buttock, then change sides.
steps.commonMistake: Do not round your back to get lower. Hinge from the hips.

steps.title: Stand up and walk it off
steps.body: Stand slowly and walk a few easy laps of the room. Stroke down the back of each hip with a flat palm as you go.
steps.sensationCue: Loose and slightly warm. Any stiffness should ease within a minute.
steps.rhythm: Slow walking pace
steps.breathCue: Easy, natural breathing
steps.voiceScript: Stand up slowly and walk a few easy laps of the room. As you walk, stroke down the back of each hip with a flat palm a few times. Everything you have just worked on needs to remember how to move.

steps.title: Check both calves first
steps.body: Look at and gently feel both calves. If one is swollen, warm, red or sore on that side only, stop now and see a doctor.
steps.sensationCue: Both calves should look and feel the same as each other.
steps.rhythm: Still — look and compare
steps.breathCue: Easy, steady breathing
steps.voiceScript: Before anything else, sit down and compare your two calves, looking at them and resting a hand on each. If one is swollen, warm, red, or painful on one side only, do not massage it. Stop here and speak to a doctor first.
steps.commonMistake: Do not massage through a one-sided swollen, hot calf. Get it checked.
steps.caution: Rubbing a calf with a possible clot is dangerous. If in doubt, skip this routine and ask a doctor.

steps.title: Circle your ankles and pump
steps.body: Lift one foot off the floor and circle the ankle slowly both ways. Then point and flex the foot ten times, and swap feet.
steps.sensationCue: Stiff at first, smoother by the end. Never a click that hurts.
steps.rhythm: One slow circle every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Easy, steady breathing
steps.voiceScript: Lift one foot off the floor and draw slow circles with your toes, five one way and five the other. Then point the foot away from you and pull it back ten times. Change feet and do the same again.
steps.commonMistake: Do not rush the circles. Big and slow beats fast and small.

steps.title: Stroke the calf upward
steps.body: Rest one ankle on the opposite knee. Wrap both hands round the calf and stroke firmly from the heel up towards the knee.
steps.sensationCue: Warm and smooth. Nothing sharp, nothing that stings.
steps.rhythm: One long stroke every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out on each stroke
steps.voiceScript: Rest one ankle across your opposite knee so you can reach the calf easily. Wrap both hands round it and stroke firmly from the heel up towards the knee, then lift off and start again from the bottom. Always stroke upwards.
steps.commonMistake: Do not stroke downwards. Work up towards the heart.
steps.caution: Stop below the crease at the back of the knee. Never press into it.

steps.title: Squeeze the belly of the calf
steps.body: Take the thickest part of the calf between your fingers and the heel of your hand. Squeeze, hold a second, let go, and move down.
steps.sensationCue: A deep, dull ache that softens as you go. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: One squeeze every two seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you squeeze
steps.voiceScript: Find the thickest part of the calf, about a hand's width below the knee. Take it between your fingers and the heel of your hand, squeeze for a second, then let go and move a little lower. Work down to the ankle and back up again.
steps.commonMistake: Do not pinch with your fingertips. Use the whole hand.

steps.title: Roll the calf on a towel
steps.body: Sit on the floor with your legs out and a rolled towel under one calf. Lift your hips slightly and slide the leg over it.
steps.sensationCue: Broad, even pressure. A good ache, never a bruised sting.
steps.rhythm: One slow pass every eight seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you roll
steps.voiceScript: Sit on the floor with your legs straight out and put a rolled towel or a foam roller under one calf. Press your hands into the floor to lift your hips a little, then slide the leg so the roll travels from the ankle to just below the knee. Cross the other ankle on top if you want more weight.
steps.commonMistake: Do not race up and down. One slow pass finds more than ten fast ones.
steps.caution: Roll only as far as just below the knee. Never on the soft crease behind it.

steps.title: Work the cord above your heel
steps.body: Pinch the firm cord above your heel between thumb and finger. Slide slowly up until it widens into muscle, then repeat.
steps.sensationCue: Firm and slightly tender. Never a hot, burning line.
steps.rhythm: One slow slide every five seconds
steps.breathCue: Steady, easy breathing
steps.voiceScript: Find the firm cord just above your heel and take it lightly between your thumb and first finger. Slide slowly upwards until it spreads out into the soft muscle of the calf. Do that four or five times, then swap legs.
steps.commonMistake: Do not squeeze the cord hard. Light and slow is right here.
steps.caution: Ease off if this area is hot, puffy, or painful when you walk.

steps.title: Thumb down the shin muscle
steps.body: Feel the sharp edge of your shin bone, then step your thumb just outside it. Press and glide slowly down the muscle to the ankle.
steps.sensationCue: Tender and stringy at first, easier on the second pass. Never bone pain.
steps.rhythm: One slow glide every six seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out on the way down
steps.voiceScript: Run a finger down the front of your shin until you feel the sharp edge of the bone. Move just to the outside of it and you are on the muscle that lifts your foot. Press with your thumb and glide slowly down towards the ankle, four or five passes on each leg.
steps.commonMistake: Do not press on the bone. It hurts and it does nothing.
steps.caution: Sharp pain along the bone itself needs rest, not pressure. See a doctor if it keeps up.

steps.title: Stretch your calf at the wall
steps.body: Put both hands on the wall and step one foot well back. Keep that leg straight, press the heel down, and hold.
steps.sensationCue: A long pull up the back of the calf. Never a pinch at the ankle.
steps.rhythm: Twenty-five seconds on each leg
steps.breathCue: Breathe out and sink a little lower
steps.voiceScript: Stand facing a wall with both hands on it. Step one foot well back, keep that leg straight, and press the heel down into the floor until you feel a long pull up the calf. Hold for twenty-five seconds, then swap legs.
steps.commonMistake: Do not let the back heel lift. The heel down is the stretch.

steps.title: Long strokes, then feet up
steps.body: Sit down and stroke both calves from ankle to knee with flat palms. Then rest your feet up on a chair for a minute.
steps.sensationCue: Light, drifting and warm. Legs should feel lighter than they did.
steps.rhythm: One slow stroke every four seconds
steps.breathCue: In for four, out for six
steps.voiceScript: Sit back down and stroke both calves with flat palms, always from the ankle up towards the knee, light and slow. Then put your feet up on a chair or a cushion and stay there for a minute. Your legs will thank you.

steps.title: Sit back and take three breaths
steps.body: Push your chair back a little and put both feet flat. Let your shoulders drop and take three slow breaths out.
steps.sensationCue: Shoulders settle a little lower. Nothing to feel yet.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: Out for longer than in
steps.voiceScript: Push your chair back from the desk and put both feet flat on the floor. Let your shoulders drop away from your ears, and take three slow breaths, each one out longer than it went in. Nobody will even notice.
steps.commonMistake: Do not skip this. Thirty still seconds sets up the rest.

steps.title: Roll your shoulders backward
steps.body: Roll both shoulders up, back and down in slow circles. Let them land lower each time, as if shrugging off a heavy coat.
steps.sensationCue: Loose and easy. No pinching at the top of the circle.
steps.rhythm: One roll every four seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as they drop
steps.voiceScript: Roll both shoulders up towards your ears, then back and down in a slow circle. Let them land a little lower each time, like you are shrugging off a heavy coat. Eight or nine slow rolls is plenty.
steps.commonMistake: Do not roll fast. Slow circles loosen more.

steps.title: Squeeze the top of your shoulder
steps.body: Reach across and grip the ridge of muscle on top of the other shoulder. Squeeze, lift slightly, let go, then swap sides.
steps.sensationCue: A deep, dull ache that eases as you squeeze. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: About one squeeze per second
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you squeeze
steps.voiceScript: Reach one hand across to the opposite shoulder and take the ridge of muscle on top between your thumb and fingers. Squeeze, lift it slightly, and let it go, like kneading dough. Twenty seconds each side, and it just looks like you are thinking.
steps.commonMistake: Do not pinch with your fingertips. Use the flat of your fingers.

steps.title: Lean your ear towards your shoulder
steps.body: Hold the side of your chair seat with one hand. Tip your ear towards the other shoulder and let the weight of your head do the work.
steps.sensationCue: A long, even pull down the side of the neck. Never a pinch.
steps.rhythm: Twenty seconds on each side
steps.breathCue: Breathe out and let it lengthen
steps.voiceScript: Take hold of the side of your chair seat with one hand, to anchor that shoulder down. Tip your ear towards the opposite shoulder and simply let the weight of your head stretch the side of your neck. Twenty slow seconds, then change hands and sides.
steps.commonMistake: Do not pull your head over with your hand. Let gravity do it.
steps.caution: Ease off straight away if you feel tingling in your arm or hand.

steps.title: Squeeze along your forearm
steps.body: Rest one forearm on the desk. Squeeze along it from elbow to wrist with your other hand, turning the arm over to do both sides.
steps.sensationCue: Firm and achy, more tender than you expect. Never tingly.
steps.rhythm: One squeeze per second, moving down
steps.breathCue: Steady, easy breathing
steps.voiceScript: Rest one forearm on the desk and squeeze along it with your other hand, starting below the elbow and working towards the wrist. Turn the arm over and do that side too. Stop before you reach the wrist crease.
steps.commonMistake: Do not squeeze the wrist crease. Stop short of it.
steps.caution: Stay off the middle of the wrist crease.

steps.title: Press into your palm and web
steps.body: Press your thumb into the middle of the other palm and make slow circles. Then squeeze the fleshy pad below the thumb.
steps.sensationCue: A satisfying, spreading ache. Never a sharp point.
steps.rhythm: Three circles, then move on
steps.breathCue: Breathe out into the pressure
steps.voiceScript: Press your thumb into the middle of your other palm and make slow circles, working outward. Then take the fleshy pad below the thumb and squeeze it between your thumb and fingers. Give each hand about twenty seconds.
steps.commonMistake: Do not dig with your thumb tip. Use the flat pad.

steps.title: Rest your palms over your eyes
steps.body: Lean your elbows on the desk and cup your palms over your closed eyes without touching them. Sit in the dark and breathe.
steps.sensationCue: Warm and dark, with no pressure on the eyes at all.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: Four slow breaths out
steps.voiceScript: Lean your elbows on the desk and cup your palms over your closed eyes, resting the edges of your hands on your cheekbones so nothing presses on the eyes. Sit in the warm dark for four slow breaths. It looks like you are reading something difficult.
steps.commonMistake: Do not press on your eyes. Rest the weight on the bone.
steps.caution: Never put pressure on the eyeball itself.

steps.title: Tuck your chin and look far
steps.body: Draw your chin straight back to make a double chin, hold five seconds, then release. Finish by looking at the furthest thing you can see.
steps.sensationCue: A stretch at the base of the skull, then easier eyes.
steps.rhythm: Five seconds on, five seconds off
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you tuck
steps.voiceScript: Draw your chin straight back, not down, so you make a bit of a double chin. Hold for five seconds and let go, three or four times. Then find the furthest thing you can see, out of a window if there is one, and look at it for twenty seconds.

steps.title: Cover them and settle
